newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 2.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
KESRI EMERGING AS CONGRESS PARLIAMENTARY CHIEF CHOICE

Former Maharashtra chief minister Sharad Pawar bowed out of the race for the leadership of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP). Sources said Pawar's decision made Congress president Sitaram Kesri's election to the post on January 3 a foregone conclusion. The Congress Working Committee (CWC) decided to set up a committee of two members to ascertain the views of Congress members of Parliament so that Kesri could be elected by consensus. Party sources, however, said supporters of former prime minister Narasimha Rao were likely to back CWC member Rajesh Pilot who had declared his candidature for the CPP leadership.
The Economic Times
ABSOLUTE EXPOSURE LIMIT FOR CORPORATES

The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) has decided to impose absolute exposure limits on all its top corporate borrowers. The step will ensure that IDBI's risks are evenly spread out and that credit-worthiness is the prime criterion for excess limits. Current guidelines limit exposure in a single company to 25 percent of an institution's net worth and upto 50 percent for a group.
FULLER BUYS OUT KCP STAKE IN INDIAN ARM

U.S. multinational Fuller International Inc has bought its Indian partner, KCP Ltd's stake in the joint venture, Fuller-KCP Ltd. The company was promoted in 1984, with both partners holding 40 percent each. Fuller secured clearance to hike its stake to 80 percent by acquiring the 40 percent holding of KCP at a price of around 135 rupees per share. Fuller-KCP is a major player in executing turnkey projects for mineral, non-mineral, mining and metallurgical industries.
BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX UP 175 POINTS

The stock markets ushered in the new year with a robust 175 point jump in the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) amid hectic buying activity from punters. The trading sentiment was perked up by assurances made by the government to announce within a fortnight policy measures aimed at reviving capital markets. The BSE sensitive index closed at 3,260.56, up 175.36 points, or 5.6 percent, over its previous close of 3,085.20 on December 24. The 50-share National Stock Exchange rose 40.45 points, or 4.4 percent, to 939.55, over the previous day's close of 899.10.
Financial Express
BPL TELECOM DROPS TWO PROJECTS

BPL Telecom has decided to shelve its video-conferencing and 64 Kbps datalink services projects. Company sources said the two projects had been dropped as the company felt that there was no market potential for them. Industry experts felt it was a radical move by BPL Telecom as video-conferencing had proved a non-starter worldwide. The decision was also seen as part of a new business strategy adopted by the company to overcome the limitations of a dull industrial climate.
Business Standard
NORMS TIGHTENED FOR TELECOM SECTOR

The Department of Telecommunications announced a new vendor rating system for bidders of equipment and services. Under the new system, weightage would be given for past performance, price and delivery schedule. This is a departure from an earlier policy under which the lowest bidder got the contract. Communications minister Beni Prasad Verma said the new policy would come into force from fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) and would not apply to existing contracts under execution.
INDUSTRY HAILS DECISION TO RELAX FOREIGN INVESTMENT

Indian industrialists welcomed the government's decision to ease restrictions on foreign direct investment and its promise to step up economic reforms. They said the government's move could spur growth. The cabinet had announced that foreign firms could take stakes of up to 74 percent in nine industrial sectors, including infrastructure, non-conventional energy and electrical software. The government had also decided to grant automatic approval to foreign companies seeking stakes of up to 51 percent in 16 other sectors.
TAX WAIVED ON STATE FIRMS' SHARES

The government has exempted investments in shares issued by public companies in the priority sector from long-term capital gains. The exemption will take effect from October 1, 1996. The capital market is set to receive a further boost as these measures provide additional tax incentives for investment in stocks. The ordinance is also being seen as part of the year-end package of measures, announced by the United Front government to kick-start the economy.
AUTO INDUSTRY SHOWS IMPRESSIVE GROWTH

Despite a general slowdown in industrial production, segments of the automobile industry registered an impressive growth in the eight-month period of April-November 1996. Total automobile production rose to 2.629 million vehicles from 2.529 million in the corresponding period in the previous year. Sales climbed to 2.582 million vehicles from 2.22 million vehicles. Going by the growth trend, experts feel the automobile industry was likely to surpass the growth of 23 percent in 1995/96 (April-March).
CUT IN SETTLEMENT RATE RULED OUT

Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) does not plan to slash the settlement rate vis-a-vis U.S. carriers to 23 cents. Instead, the state-owned telecommunication carrier will ally with its counterparts in other nations to resist the U.S. move. At present, the settlement is 80 cents per minute. VSNL plans to take up the issue together with Japan and developing world nations to put up a joint resistance.
Business Line
SKODA SCOUTING FOR PARTNER

Czech automobile manufacturer Skoda is scouting for a joint venture partner in India to manufacture its Beta range of pick-up trucks. The company is interested in setting up an assembling plant near Madras as it will source most of its major parts from Hyundai, which is putting up a plant nearby. Industry sources said Skoda has sought the help of the Tamil Nadu government for identifying a joint venture partner. Most of the auto component manufacturers and light engineering companies approached for this venture seemed to have turned down the proposal.
